_source: MMG_v19_Client_Manual_Testing_Guideline_FG15-FG20_v1.0.xlsx / Testing Guideline — pulled from the client's Drive on 2026-09-16. FG-15 'UI Widgets & Client Framework' holds 8 cases: TC-UIX-001, -003, -004, -005, -008, -009, -010, -011. All 8 are implemented; 7 pass and TC-UIX-011 fails on two menus that are not reachable.
_what_this_group_is_and_what_that_costs: Five of the eight cases are about a custom OWL widget DRAWING something — a logo beside a store name, a picture in a Store cell, a chart on a card, tick-boxes instead of a drop-down. What a widget renders is a browser fact. What an RPC client can establish is the half that decides it: the field is on the view the browser is handed, it carries the gallery's widget (logo_and_name_field, many2one_store_field, many2many_store_field, many2many_checkboxes_select_all_field, boolean_button — none of them stock Odoo, which is exactly why an upgrade can drop one silently), and the data behind it is the shape the widget expects. A blank Store cell has two causes: the column is not there (server) or the widget failed to draw (browser). This suite settles the first conclusively and says so plainly about the second. Every case carries a RESIDUAL MANUAL STEP naming what still needs eyes and why.
_one_store: TC-UIX-004 compares two cards' charts and TC-UIX-005 step 3 compares two rows' logos. This database holds ONE store. Both cases say what to do — 'record it as N/A and say why' — so those halves are recorded N/A with the store count that justifies it, rather than passed on a technicality. TC-UIX-010 step 4 (a piece on two stores in one cell) is N/A for the same reason.
_safety: TC-UIX-001 writes to the gallery's own import rule — it has to, since 'do the ticks survive a save' is a round trip — and restores the original selection both at the end of the case and again from a finally. Crons are deactivated on this instance so no import can run against a half-changed rule. TC-UIX-003 flips a shipping-carrier row's Active flag and flips it back, which is the one press the workbook asks for; neither store button is pressed, because one of them disconnects the store. TC-UIX-011's two saves write a free-text field back onto itself.

_findings.BC-FG16-001 (also fails here): TC-UIX-011 step 1i opens 'Inventory > Operations > Transfers > Deliveries'. It is not served: the branch is gated on base.group_no_one on this database while stock Odoo 19 ships it ungated. Third case to fail on this — TC-STU-006, TC-SMK-003 and now the FG-15 gate.
_findings.OBS-FG18-001 (also fails here): TC-UIX-011 step 1c opens 'E-commerce Connectors > Products > Product Variants', which is ARCHIVED (active=False) on this database, as are the Inventory and Purchase entry points to the same screen. 'Sales > Products > Product Variants' IS served, so variants themselves are on. May be a deliberate removal; only Novobi's list can say.
_findings.OBS-FG15-001: The store field on the product-mapping FORM carries invisible="1", while TC-UIX-009 step 6 says 'the store must again be shown with its picture and name'. The list columns are correct. This is the one part of TC-UIX-009 a screen has to settle — either the form shows the store some other way, or step 6's expectation does not match what was built. Recorded, not failed, because a form can legitimately present a value through another element.
_findings.OBS-FG15-002: This database holds NO shipping.method.channel rows at all, not even archived ones, so TC-UIX-003 steps 5-7 have nothing to flip. Recorded N/A rather than skipping the case: steps 2-4 are about the store's own buttons and they ran and passed.
_findings.OBS-FG15-003: product.template.active_channel_ids is a NON-STORED compute and cannot be searched on — 'Cannot convert ... to SQL because it is not stored'. TC-UIX-010 therefore starts from the stored product.channel mappings and reads the column back on the templates they name, which is also the right way round for step 6: the mappings are the source of truth the column is supposed to agree with.

TC-UIX-001.reason: PASSES, and it is the one case in this group that is not about rendering underneath. The list carries many2many_checkboxes_select_all_field (tick-boxes, not a tag box or a drop-down); its domain admits only type='fulfillment' and never mentions payment — the FAIL the workbook names — and the consequence is read off the data: every option the widget would show is a fulfilment status, while payment statuses DO exist on this platform and are correctly not offered, so the result is a filter working rather than an empty set. A changed set of ticks survives a save and re-read, and the original is put back.

TC-UIX-003.reason: PASSES. Both store buttons carry boolean_button and the fields behind them hold real states; the carrier row's control carries the same widget with archive terminology, which is what makes it read Active/Archived. Neither store button is pressed — one disconnects the store. Steps 5-7's flip is N/A: no carrier rows exist (OBS-FG15-002). The WORDING each button shows is a browser fact and is named as residual manual.

TC-UIX-004.reason: PASSES on what it can reach. The store's confirmed-order count is read as the figure step 5 reconciles against. The chart itself is painted by the browser — 'a blank space or a broken-image icon' cannot be seen from here at all — and steps 3 and 6's two-store comparison is N/A with one store.

TC-UIX-005.reason: PASSES. The Store column is the gallery's logo_and_name field carrying logo_and_name_field, and every store has a value behind it. Step 3's two-platform comparison is N/A with one store; whether the value renders as a picture, and what a store with no logo draws, is the widget's half.

TC-UIX-008.reason: PASSES. The Manage Stores list carries create=0, edit=0, delete=0 and export_xlsx=0 — which is exactly what step 4 requires of the row selection the tick-box column enables. The tick-box column itself, and the rule that clicking it selects rather than opens, are the web client's own behaviour for a non-editable list and have no attribute in the arch; that is said rather than asserted. Step 6's sign-off is a person's signature.

TC-UIX-009.reason: PASSES. The Store column is on both the Orders list and the Product Mappings list, labelled 'Store' and carrying many2one_store_field; orders both with and without a store exist, so steps 3 and 4 each have a case to be right about. The form-level question is recorded as OBS-FG15-001.

TC-UIX-010.reason: PASSES, including step 6 — which is the half of this case that can be wrong silently. A column listing the right NUMBER of stores but the wrong ones looks perfectly normal on screen; the test reconciles each sampled piece's Stores column against its actual product.channel mappings and finds them identical. Step 4 (a piece on two stores) is N/A with one store.

TC-UIX-011.reason: FAILS on two of the eleven screens — Deliveries (BC-FG16-001) and E-commerce Product Variants (OBS-FG18-001) — neither of which is served to the acting user. The other nine open and every view they pin builds; the store form's tabs are pages of one arch that built; the store card's Log entry opens scoped to its store; and BOTH saves step 3 requires complete, because 'a screen that draws but will not save is a FAIL, not a pass'. The store form is excluded from the saves exactly as step 3 instructs. Steps 4-5 (the browser Console, twice, in two browsers) are residual manual and matter more here than anywhere else in the workbook: this group is about custom OWL widgets, and one that throws in the browser leaves the server side looking healthy.
